research_scope: Base-game Parallel Quest skills from PQ 61-67 selected after duplicate screening against the canonical skill index and prior research batches.

verification_audit.method: Skill identity, class, core cost data, and PQ acquisition routes were reconciled against current Xenoverse 2 skill references and independent PQ reward guides. Exact drop probabilities and version-sensitive frame data were not inferred.
verification_audit.accuracy_note: Ultimate Finish requirements are intentionally unresolved. Earlier false values were not supported by explicit negative Ultimate-Finish evidence and have been changed to null.

records.name: Fighting Pose H
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 61 — The Cell Games Continued; reward
records.skill_description: Strike a pose to temporarily reduce incoming damage.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies Fighting Pose H as a Power Up Super costing 0 Ki with a 20-second duration. The core effect is damage reduction; exact percentage is not promoted here without a sufficiently current primary or independently corroborated source.
records.combo_notes: A defensive buff rather than an attack; it should be documented as a temporary damage-reduction state.
records.pve_notes: The temporary defensive window can be used to survive concentrated AI pressure.
records.pvp_notes: Timing the activation around predictable pressure is the key documented use case; exact current reduction values require version-specific verification.

records.name: Teleporting Vanishing Ball
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 62 — Frieza's Nightmare Returns!; reward
records.skill_description: Creates a Ki ball, teleports to the locked-on opponent, and launches the projectile at close range.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies Teleporting Vanishing Ball as a 300-Ki Ki Blast Ultimate with projectile, teleport, and long-range characteristics. The documented attack is a 15-hit sequence; exact current damage scaling and invulnerability timing are not treated as universal.
records.combo_notes: The teleporting delivery changes the attack's spacing compared with ordinary Vanishing Ball variants.
records.pve_notes: Teleportation can help connect the attack from distance and alter positioning against AI targets.
records.pvp_notes: The teleport component changes the defensive read compared with a conventional projectile; exact punish windows remain version-sensitive.

records.name: Ill Rain
records.character_source: Super Buu; Majin Buu (Gohan Absorbed) (Customize Partner); Janemba (Customize Partner); Omega Shenron (Customize Partner); Super Baby 2 (Customize Partner)
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 64 — Beerus the Impulsive; reward
records.skill_description: Launches a Ki Blast upward that scatters into three smaller projectiles.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies Ill Rain as a 100-Ki Ki Blast Super with a two-stage projectile sequence and tracking behavior. The initial projectile lingers before splitting into three smaller projectiles.
records.combo_notes: The delayed split makes it behave differently from a conventional immediate projectile and should be documented separately from Assault Rain.
records.pve_notes: The delayed multi-projectile pattern can cover multiple approach angles against AI targets.
records.pvp_notes: Tracking and delayed splitting are the main documented neutral properties; exact current tracking strength and frame data require testing.

records.name: Scissors Paper Rock
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 65 — The New Warriors; reward
records.skill_description: Enter a stance and select Rock, Scissors, or Paper; combining the three attacks creates a short three-hit sequence.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies the move as a 100-Ki Strike Super with three selectable stages. Rock performs a short strike, Scissors blinds the opponent, and Paper knocks the target away with a palm thrust.
records.combo_notes: The move stops the user in place and is not documented as a conventional combo starter; guard-break pressure is a more appropriate use category.
records.pve_notes: The selectable attacks provide different utility against AI, particularly when choosing between direct impact and the blinding effect.
records.pvp_notes: The stance and selectable follow-ups create a readable but flexible pressure option; exact startup and vanish interactions remain version-sensitive.

records.name: Candy Beam (Evasive)
records.character_source: Majin Buu (Good); Majin Buu (Good) Customize Partner; Majin CaCs
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 66 — Stop Beerus' Destruction; reward
records.skill_description: Spin and fire a pink beam that turns nearby enemies into candy temporarily.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies this as the Evasive variant of Candy Beam, costing 300 stamina and dealing no damage. Affected opponents are transformed into candy temporarily; the exact duration is not promoted as universal.
records.combo_notes: Its primary purpose is defensive escape and temporary control rather than direct damage.
records.pve_notes: The temporary transformation can create breathing room against AI and interrupt immediate pressure.
records.pvp_notes: The utility is matchup-dependent; the transformation effect should remain distinct from the Candy Beam Super variant.

records.name: Super God Fist
records.character_source: Goku; Goku (Super Saiyan God) Customize Partner; Goku (Super Saiyan 4) Customize Partner; SSGSS Goku; Trunks (Future) Customize Partner; Vegeta (Super Saiyan 4) Customize Partner; Gogeta (Super Saiyan 4) Customize Partner; Goku Black Customize Partner; Hit Customize Partner; Rosé Goku Black Customize Partner; SSGSS Vegito Customize Partner; SSGSS Gogeta Customize Partner; Majuub
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 67 — Power of a Super Saiyan God; reward
records.skill_description: Coat the right arm in Ki and charge forward with a fast punch that zooms in on the target when it connects.
records.mechanics_notes: Documentation identifies Super God Fist as a 100-Ki Strike Super with grab-like properties and a single hit. Its pseudo-grab behavior can bypass super armor, while blocking and evasive responses can still interact with it.
records.combo_notes: Its speed and pseudo-grab properties allow use after many basic attack strings; exact combo routes remain version-sensitive.
records.pve_notes: The fast single-hit attack is useful for closing short gaps and finishing basic-combo sequences.
records.pvp_notes: The pseudo-grab property changes its interaction with super armor, but it remains blockable and can be vanished in some situations.
